definition_zh: 猪；贪婪（肮脏）的人；生猪；产小猪（动词）
definition_en: a farm animal kept for its meat, or a person who eats too much or is dirty, or to give birth to pigs
core_image: 圈里那头圆滚滚的动物，鼻子拱来拱去，什么都往嘴里塞
scene: 农场里的孩子踮起脚往圈里看，那头圆滚滚的动物正用鼻子拱着食槽。The pig pushed its snout deep into the trough and ate everything.
sceneCN: 这里是「猪」（第 1 个义项：一种农场饲养的动物）；句意为那头猪把鼻子深深拱进食槽，把东西全吃光了。画面里就是那个用鼻子拱食的圆滚滚身影。

pos.zh: 猪；生猪；贪婪或肮脏的人

derivatives.zh: pig 加指小后缀 -let，义为「小猪」
pig 加 -y 构成的儿语名词，义为「猪猪」
由 piggy 与 back 合成，义为「背负；搭载」
pig 加 -ish 构成的形容词，义为「像猪一样的；贪吃的」

senses.title: A farm animal kept for meat
senses.definition: a thick-bodied farm animal with a snout, kept for its meat
senses.definitionCN: 一种身体粗壮、长着长鼻子的农场动物，为取肉而饲养
senses.example: The farmer fed the pig before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫天不亮就起来喂猪。
senses.why: Old English picg named the young animal, and the word stretched to cover the whole beast as pork became a staple.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 picg 本指小猪，随着猪肉成为主食，这个词扩大到指整头猪。

senses.title: A greedy or dirty person
senses.definition: someone who eats too much, is filthy, or behaves badly
senses.definitionCN: 吃得太多、邋遢或行为恶劣的人
senses.example: He was a pig at the buffet and left nothing for anyone else.
senses.exampleCN: 他在自助餐桌上狼吞虎咽，什么都没给别人剩下。
senses.why: The animal eats greedily and rolls in mud, so English borrowed its picture to scold a person.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物吃得贪、爱在泥里打滚，英语借它的形象来责备一个人。

senses.title: To eat greedily (pig out)
senses.definition: to eat a very large amount of food in a greedy way
senses.definitionCN: 以贪吃的方式吃下大量食物
senses.example: We pigged out on pizza after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛结束后我们放开肚皮猛吃披萨。
senses.why: The noun grew a verb by conversion: to act like the animal, mouth first.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转类成动词：像那头动物一样行动，先动嘴再说。

senses.title: To give birth to pigs
senses.definition: of a sow, to give birth to a litter of pigs
senses.definitionCN: 指母猪产下一窝小猪
senses.example: The sow pigged during the night and had ten piglets.
senses.exampleCN: 母猪夜里产崽，下了十只小猪。
senses.why: Farming speech uses the animal name itself as the verb for its own reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 农事用语直接拿动物名做动词，指它自己的繁育行为。

senses.title: Something difficult or unpleasant
senses.definition: a task or situation that is very hard or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 非常困难或令人不快的任务或处境
senses.example: The paperwork was a pig to complete on time.
senses.exampleCN: 那些文书工作很难按时完成。
senses.why: British informal speech stretches the animal's image from the person to the burden he carries.
senses.whyCN: 英式口语把这种动物的形象从「人」延伸到「他背负的重担」。

senses.title: Pig iron or metal mass
senses.definition: crude iron moulded into blocks, or the metal itself
senses.definitionCN: 铸成块状的粗铁或这种金属本身
senses.example: The old furnace poured pig iron into long moulds.
senses.exampleCN: 旧高炉把生铁浇进长条铸模。
senses.why: The moulds looked like a row of suckling pigs, so ironworkers named the metal after them.
senses.whyCN: 铸模排成一排像吃奶的小猪，冶铁工人便用它们给这种金属命名。

senses.title: A police officer (slang)
senses.definition: an insulting slang word for a police officer
senses.definitionCN: 对警察的侮辱性俚语称呼
senses.example: The crowd shouted at the officers as the van passed.
senses.exampleCN: 警车驶过时人群朝警员喊骂。
senses.why: The insult recycles the same picture: fat, dirty, greedy — words aimed at the uniform rather than the man.
senses.whyCN: 这层侮辱义复用同一形象：肥、脏、贪——矛头指向制服而非具体的人。

intro.en: Pig is an Old English word for the young of the swine, whose deeper roots are uncertain; the verb and the insulting uses grew inside English.
intro.cn: pig 是古英语里对猪幼崽的称呼，更深的来源不确定；动词义和辱骂用法都在英语内部长出来。

items.en: Picg appeared in Old English for a young pig, but no earlier Indo-European form can be safely traced.
items.cn: 古英语 picg 已见，指小猪，但更早的印欧词形无法可靠追溯。

items.en: The word widened from the piglet to the whole animal while the older swine kept the formal place.
items.cn: 词义从小猪扩大到整头猪，更古老的 swine 保留在正式场合。

items.en: Speakers turned the noun into a verb for greedy eating and for the sow farrowing, with no new ending added.
items.cn: 说话人把名词直接用作动词，指贪吃和母猪产崽，不加任何新词尾。

items.en: In ironworks the blocks of crude iron were likened to a litter of pigs, giving pig iron.
items.cn: 在冶铁业里，粗铁块被比作一窝小猪，于是有了 pig iron。

items.en: British informal English also uses a pig for a hard task and, as an insult, for a policeman.
items.cn: 英式非正式英语还用 a pig 指难办的事，并作俚语辱骂警察。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pig word family; the near-meaning group gathers words for the farm animal and for greedy eating.
note.cn: 形近组收 pig 的词族；近义组收指这种农场动物以及贪吃的词。

entries.definition: A baby pig, built with the small-size ending -let.
entries.definitionCN: 用指小词尾 -let 构成的小猪。

entries.definition: The nursery form of pig, used by and with children.
entries.definitionCN: pig 的儿语形式，用于孩子之间或对孩子说。

entries.definition: Greedy or dirty in the manner of a pig.
entries.definitionCN: 像猪一样贪吃或邋遢的。

entries.definition: The older formal word for the pig family of animals.
entries.definitionCN: 指猪类动物更古老正式的词。

entries.definition: A pig raised for meat, especially in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 供食用的猪，美式英语尤其常用。

entries.definition: An adult female pig, the one that farrows.
entries.definitionCN: 成年的母猪，即产崽的那一头。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and old, so memory works best on the animal's picture and on the fixed phrases built from it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词又短又老，记忆最好借助动物的形象和由它组成的固定短语。

normal.en: Old English picg — just three sound shapes long, one of the shortest animal names in the language.
normal.cn: 古英语 picg——只有三个音段，是英语里最短的动物名之一。

normal.en: Pig out keeps the animal inside the phrase: to eat the way a pig eats.
normal.cn: pig out 把动物留在短语里：像猪那样吃。

normal.en: Guinea pig is neither from Guinea nor a pig — a good reminder that compounds can mislead.
normal.cn: guinea pig 既非来自几内亚也不是猪——复合词会骗人。

normal.en: Pig iron comes from moulds shaped like a litter of suckling pigs.
normal.cn: pig iron 来自像一窝吃奶小猪的铸模。

normal.en: Piggyback rides on the back, exactly where a child carries a piglet home.
normal.cn: piggyback 趴在背上，正是小孩抱小猪回家时放它的地方。

abstract.en: A round pink body pushing its snout through mud — the body is the meaning.
abstract.cn: 一个粉色的圆身子把鼻子拱进泥里——身体本身就是意义。

abstract.en: The trough emptied to the last grain: greed made visible.
abstract.cn: 食槽被吃得一粒不剩：贪婪变得看得见。

abstract.en: From piglet to pig iron, the word stretches from a small breathing animal to a cold block of metal.
abstract.cn: 从小猪到生铁，这个词从一只会呼吸的小动物延伸到一块冰冷的金属。

examples.en: The pig rooted around in the straw for hours.
examples.cn: 那头猪在稻草里拱了好几个小时。

examples.en: Stop pigging out and save some cake for your sister.
examples.cn: 别猛吃了，给你妹妹留点蛋糕。

examples.en: He made a real pig of himself at the feast.
examples.cn: 他在宴席上吃相实在难看。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「屁个」——那头猪放了个屁个屁，圆滚滚地拱进食槽；pig 就是猪。

root: pig 源自古英语 picg（小猪），更早的印欧词形来源不确定；动词义与辱骂义均为英语内部由名词形象引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: One short word covers the animal, the person who behaves like it, the verbs of eating and farrowing, the hard task, the crude iron and the street insult.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个短词覆盖了动物本身、像它那样的人、吃与产崽的动词、难办的事、粗铁块和街头辱骂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pink snout pushing into the trough and swallowing everything.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个粉色长鼻子拱进食槽，把什么都吞下。

branches.en: the round beast in the pen
branches.cn: 圈里那头圆滚滚的牲畜

branches.en: the guest who empties the buffet
a hand reaching for a fourth helping
the paperwork nobody wants to face
from the straw of the pen to the moulds of the furnace
branches.cn: 从圈里的稻草到高炉的铸模

intro.en: Pig is a bare Old English noun; everything else in the family is built by English endings, compounds and conversion.
intro.cn: pig 是一个光秃秃的古英语名词；词族里其余成员都靠英语词尾、复合和转类构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributed nothing here; the whole family is Germanic and English-made.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这里没有贡献；整个词族都是日耳曼源、英语自造。

derivatives.zh: pig 加 -let 构成，义为「小猪」
pig 加 -ish 构成，义为「像猪一样的」

definition_zh: 堆；一堆； pile ；堆放；桩；柱；涌出
definition_en: objects lying one on another in a mass, or to put things in such a mass, or a heavy column driven into the ground
core_image: 东西一件压一件，越叠越高，摇摇欲坠
scene: 搬家那天，妈妈把书一本一本摞在门口，摞到快有人那么高。The books stood in a tall pile by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「堆；一堆」（第 1 个义项：叠在一起的物品）；句意为书摞成高高的一堆立在门口。画面里就是一摞顶到下巴的书。

pos.zh: 堆放；堆叠；（pile) （非正式）涌进涌出

derivatives.zh: pile 加 -ing 构成，义为「打桩；桩群」
pile 与 up 的复合形容词，义为「堆积的」
与 pile 同源的姊妹词形，义为「塔架；桥塔」

senses.title: A mass of things lying one on another
senses.definition: objects stacked loosely on top of each other
senses.definitionCN: 松散地叠在一起的物品
senses.example: A pile of letters waited on his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆信件堆在他的桌上等处理。
senses.why: Latin pila meant a pier or column, and the stone sense became the picture for things resting on each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pila 指桥墩或柱，石头意象变成了东西彼此叠压的画面。

senses.title: A large quantity
senses.definition: a very large amount of something, especially money
senses.definitionCN: 很大数量，尤指金钱
senses.example: She made a pile selling handmade jewellery online.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠网上卖手工首饰赚了一大笔。
senses.why: A stack grows until it becomes abundance: the picture of many objects turns into the idea of much.
senses.whyCN: 一堆东西越堆越多，直到变成「丰盛」：从许多件东西的画面转出「大量」的概念。

senses.title: A heavy column driven into the ground
senses.definition: a long heavy beam of wood, steel or concrete driven into the ground to support a building
senses.definitionCN: 打入地下的木、钢或混凝土长柱，用于支撑建筑
senses.example: Workers drove a concrete pile into the riverbed.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把一根混凝土桩打进河床。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original Latin image of a pier standing on stone: a column holding weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了拉丁语原意中「石上立柱」的形象：一根承重的柱。

senses.title: To put things in a heap
senses.definition: to put things on top of each other in a loose mass
senses.definitionCN: 把东西松散地叠放在一起
senses.example: He piled the dirty dishes beside the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 他把脏盘子堆在水槽边。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb by conversion: to make a pile out of things.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转类成动词：把东西弄成一堆。

senses.title: To move quickly in a crowd
senses.titleCN: 涌进涌出（pile into / out of）
senses.definition: to move quickly and in large numbers into or out of a place
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人快速涌进或涌出某处
senses.example: The team piled out of the bus and onto the field.
senses.exampleCN: 全队从车上涌出来跑向球场。
senses.why: People pressed together like objects in a heap, so the heap picture covers movement too.
senses.whyCN: 人们挤在一起，就像堆里的东西，堆的画面也覆盖了移动。

senses.title: To accumulate over time
senses.definition: to increase gradually until there are too many
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐增加直到多到应付不过来
senses.example: Unpaid bills piled up during her illness.
senses.exampleCN: 她生病期间未付的账单越积越多。
senses.why: One object on another, day after day, until the heap can no longer be managed.
senses.whyCN: 一件压一件，日复一日，直到那堆东西再也无法应付。

senses.title: To add pressure or blame
senses.definition: to add more criticism, work or pressure to what already exists
senses.definitionCN: 在已有基础上追加批评、工作或压力
senses.example: The tabloids piled on after the scandal broke.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻曝光后小报们火上浇油。
senses.why: Adding one more thing to a heap is exactly what a critic does to a reputation.
senses.whyCN: 往堆上再添一件东西，正是批评者对名声做的事。

intro.en: Pile comes through Old French from Latin pila, a pier or column of stone; the heap meaning grew from the column picture, and modern building took the column back as a technical sense.
intro.cn: pile 经古法语来自拉丁语 pila（石桥墩或柱）；「堆」义从柱子的形象长出来，而现代建筑又把「柱」收回去当专业义项。

items.en: Pila meant a stone pillar or a mole built into the sea.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pila 指石柱或伸入海中的堤。

items.en: Pile kept the column meaning as it passed into French.
items.cn: 进入法语后 pile 保留了柱子的意思。

items.en: English took pile for both the column and, by image, the heap of things stacked like stones.
items.cn: 英语借入 pile，既指柱子，也借其形象指像石头一样叠起来的堆。

items.en: Engineering revived the column as a beam driven into soil to carry weight.
items.cn: 工程学把柱义复活为打入土中承重的桩。

items.en: Informal English made a pile for making a fortune and pile up for bills and debts accumulating.
items.cn: 非正式英语用 make a pile 指发大财，用 pile up 指账单债务的累积。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Latin column family and a false friend; the near-meaning group holds words for heaps and stacking.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「柱」词族和一个假朋友；近义组收指堆与叠放的词。

entries.definition: A tall upright column supporting a building or a person's role.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑建筑或承担角色的立柱。

entries.definition: A tower carrying cables or marking a road, from the same Latin stone image.
entries.definitionCN: 承载线缆或标示道路的塔架，源于同一拉丁石柱意象。

entries.definition: A structure from shore into water; spelling looks close but the source differs.
entries.definitionCN: 从岸边伸入水中的结构；拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: A disorderly mass of things thrown together.
entries.definitionCN: 乱扔在一起的杂乱一堆。

entries.definition: A neatly arranged pile, often of the same items.
entries.definitionCN: 码放整齐的一叠，通常是同类物品。

entries.definition: A rounded heap of earth or small objects.
entries.definitionCN: 土或小物件的圆堆。

normalIntro.en: The word hides two pictures — a stack of things and a column of stone — and both help memory.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词藏着两幅画面——一堆东西和一根石柱——都有助于记忆。

normal.en: Latin pila, stone pillar; picture a pillar of books standing on the desk.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pila 是石柱；想象桌上一摞立起来的书柱。

normal.en: Pile up works for laundry, bills and snow: anything that grows one layer at a time.
normal.cn: pile up 可用于脏衣、账单和积雪：任何一层层长起来的东西。

normal.en: Pile into the car keeps the heap picture: bodies squeezed like luggage.
normal.cn: pile into the car 保留堆的画面：人像行李一样挤在一起。

normal.en: Make a pile is British money slang — a pile of banknotes, not of stones.
normal.cn: make a pile 是英式金钱俚语——指的是一叠钞票，不是石头。

normal.en: A foundation pile goes down, a laundry pile goes up — one word, two directions.
normal.cn: 地基桩往下打，脏衣堆往上摞——一个词，两个方向。

abstract.en: Gravity does the stacking: things fall onto things, and a pile is born.
abstract.cn: 重力完成堆叠：东西落在东西上，一堆就诞生了。

abstract.en: A debt grows invisibly, but a pile grows visibly — the word forces you to see the burden.
abstract.cn: 债务无形地生长，堆却看得见——这个词逼你看见负担。

abstract.en: From stone pier to paper stack, pile measures everything that holds something up by mass.
abstract.cn: 从石墩到纸堆，pile 丈量一切靠体量托住东西的东西。

examples.en: She sorted the washing into three piles.
examples.cn: 她把要洗的衣服分成三堆。

examples.en: Work kept piling up before the holidays.
examples.cn: 假期之前工作越积越多。

examples.en: The bridge rests on concrete piles sunk deep in mud.
examples.cn: 大桥坐落在深插泥中的混凝土桩上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派哦」——快递员派件派哦，门口堆成小山；pile 就是一堆。

root: 拉丁语 pila（石柱、堤）经古法语 pile 进入中古英语；「堆」义由石柱叠石的形象引申，工程义「桩」则保留柱的本义。

sensesIntro.en: A single stone image forks into two lines: the vertical column that carries a building, and the loose heap that anything falling makes.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个石头的意象分出两条线：承载建筑的竖直柱，和任何东西落下时形成的那堆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things resting one on another, whether stacked by hands or sunk by machines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件压着一件，无论是人手摞的还是机器打的。

branches.en: letters lying on a desk in layers
branches.cn: 一层层躺在桌上的信件

branches.en: banknotes counted in thick stacks
branches.cn: 厚厚一叠一叠数着的钞票

branches.en: a beam disappearing into river mud
players squeezing through one door
branches.cn: 球员们从一扇门里挤出来

branches.en: the same heap, made in a minute or a year
branches.cn: 同一堆东西，一分钟或一年堆成

intro.en: Pile itself is unanalysable, but English builds freely on it with particles and compounds.
intro.cn: pile 本身不可再分析，但英语用小词和复合词在它上面自由构词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root pila left few direct relatives in English; most of the family was built inside English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 pila 在英语里留下的直接同源词不多；词族大部分在英语内部构成。

latinEntries.meaning: stone pillar, pier
latinEntries.meaningCN: 石柱；堤

derivatives.zh: pile 加 -ing 构成，义为「打桩；桩基」
复合形容词，义为「堆积的」

definition_zh: 药丸；药片；避孕药；讨厌的人（非正式）
definition_en: a small solid round piece of medicine that you swallow whole
core_image: 一颗能整个吞下的小圆球，苦味藏在糖衣里
scene: 护士倒了一杯温水递过去，示意她仰头把那颗小圆球咽下去。She swallowed the pill with a sip of water.
sceneCN: 这里是「药丸」（第 1 个义项：小粒固体内服药）；句意为她就着一口水把药丸咽下。画面里就是那颗顺着喉咙滑下去的小圆球。

pos.zh: 药丸；药片；口服避孕药；讨厌鬼

derivatives.zh: pill 与 box 的复合词，义为「药丸盒；盒式帽」
旧式复合词，义为「制药者；药剂师」
罕用派生词，义为「用药丸的人」

senses.title: A small round dose of medicine
senses.definition: a small solid piece of medicine made to be swallowed whole
senses.definitionCN: 制成小粒、可整颗吞服的固体药物
senses.example: The doctor prescribed one pill each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 医生开了药，每天早晨一粒。
senses.why: Latin pilula is a little ball, and the medicine takes the shape of its name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pilula 意为小球，药采用了它名字所指的形状。

senses.title: Oral contraception
senses.definition: the pill, a daily medicine that prevents pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 指「the pill」，每日服用以避孕的药
senses.example: She started taking the pill in her twenties.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十多岁开始服用避孕药。
senses.why: One medicine became so common that its common noun with the article names it alone.
senses.whyCN: 一种药太常用，以致带定冠词的普通名词单独指它。

senses.title: Something unpleasant that must be accepted
senses.titleCN: 难以接受的事（a bitter pill）
senses.definition: a fact or loss that is hard to accept
senses.definitionCN: 难以接受的事实或损失
senses.example: Losing to a rival team was a bitter pill to swallow.
senses.exampleCN: 输给宿敌令人难以接受。
senses.why: The taste of medicine transfers to the taste of bad news.
senses.whyCN: 药的苦味转移到了坏消息的味道上。

senses.title: An annoying person
senses.definition: an annoying or tiresome person, American informal
senses.definitionCN: 令人恼火或厌烦的人，美式非正式
senses.example: Her little brother can be a real pill on long drives.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟长途坐车时实在烦人。
senses.why: The person becomes the medicine you are forced to swallow again and again.
senses.whyCN: 这个人变成了你不得不一次次吞下的那剂药。

senses.title: To form into pills
senses.definition: to roll medicine or food into small round pieces
senses.definitionCN: 把药物或食物搓成小圆粒
senses.example: The pharmacist pilled the herb paste by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师手工把药膏搓成丸。
senses.why: The noun names the result, and the verb names the making of it.
senses.whyCN: 名词指成品，动词指把它做出来的过程。

senses.title: A pellet or ball of anything
senses.definition: a small ball of any substance, such as lint or dough
senses.definitionCN: 任何物质的小球粒，如毛球或面团球
senses.example: Sweaters collect little pills after many washes.
senses.exampleCN: 毛衣多次洗涤后会起小球。
senses.why: The shape, not the substance, carries the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 承载意义的是形状，而非材料。

senses.title: Pill-popping, habitual medication
senses.definition: frequent casual use of pills, often without medical need
senses.definitionCN: 频繁随意服药，往往并无医疗必要
senses.example: The film shows a pill-popping society unable to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 影片描绘了一个靠药丸度日、无法入睡的社会。
senses.why: When doses multiply, the pill stops being a cure and becomes a habit.
senses.whyCN: 当服用次数倍增，药丸不再是治疗，而成习惯。

intro.en: Pill comes from Latin pilula, a little ball, a diminutive of pila, the same ball-shaped stone that gave pile; the path ran through Middle Dutch and Middle English.
intro.cn: pill 来自拉丁语 pilula（小球），是 pila 的指小形式，与 pile 同源；路径经由中古荷兰语与中古英语。

items.en: Pila meant a ball or pillar; pilula, its diminutive, meant a little ball.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pila 指球或柱；其指小形式 pilula 意为小球。

items.en: Middle Dutch pile and Middle Low German pille carried the medicine sense northward.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pile 与中古低地德语 pille 把药丸义带向北方。

items.en: Pill appeared in fourteenth-century English for a rolled medicine.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语已用 pill 指搓制的药丸。

items.en: The idiom a bitter pill and the verb to pill grew inside English.
items.cn: a bitter pill 的习语和动词 to pill 都在英语内部生长。

items.en: The twentieth century added the pill for contraception and pillbox hats and cases.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添了 the pill（避孕药）以及 pillbox 帽和药盒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the ball-shaped family and two deceiving neighbours; the near-meaning group gathers dosage words.
note.cn: 形近组收球形词族和两个易混词；近义组收剂型用语。

entries.definition: A small pill, keeping the Latin diminutive almost unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 小药丸，几乎原样保留拉丁指小形式。

entries.definition: A heap or column; the shared Latin image is a ball or stone, but the words took separate paths.
entries.definitionCN: 堆或柱；共享拉丁意象但两词各自分化。

entries.definition: A small pressed ball of material; only the shape matches.
entries.definitionCN: 压制成的小球粒；仅形状相似，词源不同。

entries.definition: A flat pressed dose of medicine, not round.
entries.definitionCN: 压制的扁平药片，不呈圆形。

entries.definition: A soluble case holding medicine, from Latin little box.
entries.definitionCN: 装有药物的可溶胶囊，源自拉丁语「小盒」。

entries.definition: The measured amount of medicine taken at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 一次服用的定量药物。

normalIntro.en: One picture does the work: a small ball travelling down the throat.
normalIntro.cn: 一幅画面足矣：一颗小球顺喉而下。

normal.en: Latin pilula is literally little ball — the pill is a ball you swallow.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pilula 字面即小球——药丸就是你吞下的球。

normal.en: Pill and pile share the Latin pila; one shrank to a ball, the other grew into a heap.
normal.cn: pill 与 pile 共享拉丁 pila；一个缩成小球，一个堆成大堆。

normal.en: The pill without a number still means one specific medicine in modern speech.
normal.cn: 现代口语中，不带数字的 the pill 特指一种药。

normal.en: A bitter pill to swallow matches taste to truth: bad facts taste like medicine.
normal.cn: a bitter pill to swallow 把味道对上事实：坏消息尝起来像药。

normal.en: Pills on a sweater are also little balls — the shape meaning never left.
normal.cn: 毛衣上的毛球也是小球——形状义从未离开。

abstract.en: The smallest container of relief: an entire cure in one round shell.
abstract.cn: 最小的缓解容器：整个疗法装进一个圆壳。

abstract.en: Swallowing is agreeing: the idiom makes acceptance an act of the throat.
abstract.cn: 吞咽即接受：习语把「接受」变成喉咙的动作。

abstract.en: From the pharmacist's hand to the sweater's cuff, the little ball keeps rolling through the language.
abstract.cn: 从药剂师的手到毛衣的袖口，小球在语言里一路滚下去。

examples.en: Take one pill after every meal.
examples.cn: 每餐后服一粒药。

examples.en: The defeat was a bitter pill for the whole team.
examples.cn: 这场失败让全队难以接受。

examples.en: My old sweater is covered in little pills.
examples.cn: 我的旧毛衣起了一层小球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮欧」——皮蛋大小的药丸一口吞下，皮欧一声就进肚；pill 就是药丸。

root: 拉丁语 pila（球、柱）的指小形式 pilula（小球）经中古荷兰语进入中古英语成为 pill；核心意象始终是小圆球。

sensesIntro.en: The little ball of Latin grows through medicine into money slang, moral idiom, a nuisance person and even the fuzz on a sweater.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁的小球经由医药长出金钱俚语、道德习语、讨厌鬼，甚至毛衣上的毛球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smooth little ball that goes down whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗整个咽下的光滑小球。

branches.en: a round dose in the palm of a hand
a packet opened every morning
branches.cn: 每天早晨拆开的一板药

branches.en: a face forcing down hard news
a back-seat brother asking questions nonstop
branches.cn: 后座上问个不停的弟弟

branches.en: the same ball of lint and of medicine

intro.en: The word family is small: the Latin diminutive plus a few English compounds.
intro.cn: 词族很小：拉丁指小形式加若干英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pilula stands behind the whole group; no other Latin terms are needed.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族背后是拉丁语 pilula；无需其他拉丁词。

latinEntries.meaning: little ball
latinEntries.meaningCN: 小球

derivatives.zh: 复合词，义为「药丸盒」

definition_zh: 飞行员；领航员；试点；试验性的；驾驶（飞机）
definition_en: a person who flies or steers a craft, or a trial project to test an idea, or to steer a ship through dangerous waters
core_image: 一只手稳稳把住操纵杆，把船或飞机带过最险的一段水路
scene: 驾驶舱里，机长扫了一眼仪表，推动油门准备起飞。The pilot pulled back the control column and the plane climbed.
sceneCN: 这里是「飞行员」（第 1 个义项：驾驶航空器的人）；句意为飞行员拉起操纵杆，飞机爬升。画面里就是那只稳住操纵杆的手。

pos.zh: 驾驶（飞机船舶）；带领；试验

derivatives.zh: pilot 加 -age 构成，义为「引航；引航费」
co- 与 pilot 复合，义为「副驾驶员」
auto- 与 pilot 复合，义为「自动驾驶仪」
pilot 加 -less 构成，义为「无人驾驶的」

senses.title: A person who flies aircraft
senses.definition: someone trained to operate an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 经训练能操纵航空器的人
senses.example: The pilot announced the descent into Shanghai.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员广播即将下降降落上海。
senses.why: The steersman of ships was recycled for the steersman of new flying machines.
senses.whyCN: 船只的操舵者被重新借用于新式飞行器的操舵者。

senses.title: A guide through dangerous waters
senses.definition: a specialist who takes ships safely through a port or channel
senses.definitionCN: 带领船舶安全进出港口或航道的技术人员
senses.example: A local pilot boarded to guide the tanker into harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 引水员登船，引导油轮进港。
senses.why: The original Italian sense: the man who knows the local water and holds the helm there.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的意大利语词义：熟悉当地水道、在船头掌舵的人。

senses.title: A trial project
senses.definition: a small first attempt used to test whether a plan works
senses.definitionCN: 为检验方案是否可行而做的小规模首次尝试
senses.example: The city ran a pilot before extending the scheme citywide.
senses.exampleCN: 全市推广前，该市先做了试点。
senses.why: The steersman tests the channel first; a project also tests the water before full commitment.
senses.whyCN: 引水员先探水路；项目在全面铺开前也先试水。

senses.title: Experimental, serving as a test
senses.definition: describing something done as a trial
senses.definitionCN: 形容作为试验而进行的事物
senses.example: The hospital opened a pilot clinic with twelve beds.
senses.exampleCN: 医院开设了一个只有十二张床位的试验门诊。
senses.why: The trial sense turns into an adjective placed before the noun it tests.
senses.whyCN: 试验义转成形容词，置于它所检验的名词之前。

senses.title: To steer or control a craft
senses.definition: to operate an aircraft, ship or spacecraft
senses.definitionCN: 操纵飞机、船只或航天器
senses.example: She piloted the glider through the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 她驾驶滑翔机穿山谷而过。
senses.why: The person's job becomes the act itself by conversion.
senses.whyCN: 名词转类，人的工作变成动作本身。

senses.title: To lead a person or plan
senses.definition: to guide someone or something through a difficult process
senses.definitionCN: 引导人或事渡过艰难过程
senses.example: He piloted the bill through parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 他推动法案在议会获得通过。
senses.why: Steering a boat through rocks is extended to steering any plan through obstacles.
senses.whyCN: 驾船避礁引申为推动任何计划越过障碍。

senses.title: A constant small flame
senses.definition: a small continuous flame that lights a burner when needed
senses.definitionCN: 为随时点燃而持续燃烧的小火苗
senses.example: The boiler would not start because its pilot had gone out.
senses.exampleCN: 锅炉打不着火，因为长明小火熄了。
senses.why: The small flame stands by, ready to steer the fire onward.
senses.whyCN: 小火苗随时待命，引导大火燃起。

intro.en: Pilot comes from Italian pilota, probably from Greek pedal skill — one school links it to pēdon, an oar or helm, though the early history is debated.
intro.cn: pilot 来自意大利语 pilota，一般认为与希腊语的桨舵技能相关——一种说法把它联系到 pēdon（桨或舵），早期历史尚有争论。

items.en: Pēdon meant an oar or helm; scholars generally but not certainly connect it to the later word.
items.cn: pēdon 指桨或舵；学者一般认为（但非确证）它与后来的词相连。

items.en: Pilota appears in the Renaissance for the man who steers a ship.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期意大利语 pilota 已指驾船掌舵的人。

items.en: French pilote carried the word north in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪法语 pilote 把这个词带往北方。

items.en: English took pilot for ship guides, then transferred it to aviators as flight began.
items.cn: 英语用 pilot 指引水员，航空兴起后又转指飞行员。

items.en: The twentieth century added trial projects, pilot lights and autopilot.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添试点项目、长明小火和自动驾驶仪。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the steering family; the near-meaning group collects people who guide or drive.
note.cn: 形近组收掌舵词族；近义组收引导或驾驶之人。

entries.definition: A device that flies the plane without a hand on the controls.
entries.definitionCN: 无需人手操控便能驾驶飞机的装置。

entries.definition: The second flier who shares the cockpit duties.
entries.definitionCN: 分担驾驶舱职责的第二位飞行者。

entries.definition: The work and the fee of guiding ships into port.
entries.definitionCN: 引航工作及其收费。

entries.definition: The crew member who plans the route rather than holds the controls.
entries.definitionCN: 规划航线而非直接操控的机组成员。

entries.definition: The person at the helm of a boat.
entries.definitionCN: 在舵位上驾船的人。

entries.definition: The captain of a small vessel, informal.
entries.definitionCN: 小船的船长，非正式。

normalIntro.en: Remember the hand on the helm, then let the word climb from the deck of a ship into the cockpit.
normalIntro.cn: 记住握舵的手，再让这个词从甲板爬进驾驶舱。

normal.en: Italian pilota held the helm first; aviators borrowed the title two centuries later.
normal.cn: 意大利语 pilota 先掌舵；飞行员在两个世纪后借用了这个头衔。

normal.en: A pilot project tests the waters — exactly what a harbour pilot does every day.
normal.cn: 试点项目是在试水——正是引水员每天做的事。

normal.en: Pilot light is the tiny flame that never sleeps in old stoves and boilers.
normal.cn: pilot light 是旧炉子和锅炉里长明的小火苗。

normal.en: Autopilot can also describe a day you spend on mental cruise control.
normal.cn: autopilot 也可以形容你大脑挂上定速巡航的一天。

normal.en: Pilot episode is the TV sample that tests whether a series deserves a channel slot.
normal.cn: 试播集是检验剧集是否值得占据时段的样片。

abstract.en: Every new journey needs one steady hand to take the first turn.
abstract.cn: 每段新旅程都需要一只稳手完成第一个转弯。

abstract.en: The pilot knows the rocks before the rocks are visible — knowledge as navigation.
abstract.cn: 引水员在礁石可见之前就知道它们——知识即导航。

abstract.en: From oar to joystick, the word tracks humanity's history of steering machines.
abstract.cn: 从桨到操纵杆，这个词记录了人类操控机器的历史。

examples.en: The pilot landed the plane in heavy fog.
examples.cn: 飞行员在大雾中让飞机着陆。

examples.en: The school launched a pilot scheme for online homework.
examples.cn: 学校启动了线上作业的试点方案。

examples.en: He piloted the negotiations to a fair ending.
examples.cn: 他把谈判引向一个公平的结局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派勒特」——派个舵手来掌舵，派勒特就是领航的飞行员；pilot 即引航者。

root: 一般认为源自意大利语 pilota，可追溯至希腊语 pēdon（桨、舵），早期演变存争论；词义由驾船引航延伸到航空与试验义。

sensesIntro.en: One steersman branches into aviators, harbour guides, trial projects, small flames and even bills steered through parliament.
sensesIntro.cn: 一位操舵者分出飞行员、引水员、试点项目、长明小火，乃至在议会里被推动的法案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady hand on the helm taking a craft through the risky stretch.
core.cn: 核心意象：稳稳把舵的手，带航器驶过最险一段。

branches.en: a figure in uniform at the controls
branches.cn: 在操纵台前穿制服的身影

branches.en: a launch drawing near the waiting tanker
a small clinic opened for one winter
branches.cn: 只开了一个冬天的小门诊

branches.en: a bill carried clause by clause
branches.cn: 一条一条被推动通过的法案

branches.en: the same hand, first the job then the act
branches.cn: 同一只手：先是职务，再是动作

intro.en: Pilot combines freely with prefixes and particles to name every kind of steering.
intro.cn: pilot 可与前缀和小词自由组合，命名各种驾驶方式。

latinIntro.en: The assumed Greek helm-root left no other Latin relatives; the family is built inside European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 假定的希腊舵根没有留下其他拉丁同族词；词族在欧洲语言内部构成。

derivatives.zh: pilot 加 -age，义为「引航；引航费」
auto- 复合，义为「自动驾驶仪」
pilot 加 -less，义为「无人驾驶的」

definition_zh: 大头针；别针；销钉；插脚；别住；钉住；固定
definition_en: a small pointed metal fastener, or a part of a machine or plug, or to fasten something with such a pin
core_image: 一枚又细又尖的小金属针，把两样东西死死别在一起
scene: 她把写着座位的纸条别在校服领口，怕自己又忘了教室。She used a pin to fix the note to her collar.
sceneCN: 这里是「别住」（第 5 个义项：用别针把东西固定）；句意是她用别针把纸条固定在领口。画面里就是那枚把纸条按在布上的小针。

derivatives.zh: pin 加 -ing 构成，义为「钉固；固定」
与拉丁钳形词相关，义为「钳子；钳形运动」
pin 与 head 复合，义为「针头；极小的东西」
pin 与 point 复合，义为「精确定位」

senses.title: A small pointed metal fastener
senses.definition: a thin pointed piece of metal with a head, used to hold things together
senses.definitionCN: 带针头的细尖金属，用来把东西固定在一起
senses.example: The tailor held the fold in place with a pin.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝用一枚别针把褶子固定住。
senses.why: Latin pinna meant a feather, then a pointed quill, then anything sharp and thin.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pinna 指羽毛，继而指羽茎，再引申为任何尖细之物。

senses.title: A pin as a safety fastener
senses.definition: a pin with a coiled spring and a protective cover over the point
senses.definitionCN: 带弹簧圈和护针帽的别针
senses.example: A safety pin held the torn strap.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚安全别针别住了撕破的带子。
senses.why: The invention adds protection to the naked point of the pin.
senses.whyCN: 这项发明给裸露的针尖加了保护。

senses.title: A machine or plug pin
senses.definition: a small metal rod that holds machine parts together or connects a plug
senses.definitionCN: 固定机器部件或连接插头的小金属杆
senses.example: One bent pin stopped the plug from fitting.
senses.exampleCN: 一根弯了的插脚让插头插不进去。
senses.why: The sharp slender shape transfers from cloth to machinery.
senses.whyCN: 尖细的形状从布料转移到机械上。

senses.title: A personal identification code
senses.definition: a secret number used with a bank card or device
senses.definitionCN: 配合银行卡或设备使用的保密数字
senses.example: She changed her bank pin after the phone was stolen.
senses.exampleCN: 手机被盗后她改了银行卡密码。
senses.why: The acronym PIN was later spelled like the word, and the meanings fused.
senses.whyCN: 缩写 PIN 后来拼成与该词相同，两义融合。

senses.title: To fasten with a pin
senses.definition: to attach something using a pin or similar pointed object
senses.definitionCN: 用别针或类似尖物把东西固定
senses.example: He pinned the medal onto his jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把勋章别在夹克上。
senses.why: The tool gives its name to the act done with it.
senses.whyCN: 工具把自己的名字给了用它完成的动作。

senses.title: To hold someone down
senses.definition: to press a person or animal so they cannot move
senses.definitionCN: 压制人或动物使之无法动弹
senses.example: The wrestler pinned his opponent to the mat.
senses.exampleCN: 摔跤手把对手按在垫子上。
senses.why: The needle fixes cloth; the same fixing force fixes a body.
senses.whyCN: 针固定布料；同样的固定之力固定身体。

senses.title: To identify precisely
senses.definition: to establish a fact, cause or position exactly
senses.definitionCN: 准确查明事实、原因或位置
senses.example: Doctors finally pinned down the cause of the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 医生终于查明了疼痛的原因。
senses.why: A pin marks one exact point; the idiom transfers that to facts.
senses.whyCN: 针标记一个精确点；习语把这一点转移到事实。

intro.en: Pin comes from Latin pinna or penna, a feather, whose quill stem gave the sense of a pointed shaft; Middle English took the word from Old French.
intro.cn: pin 源自拉丁语 pinna 或 penna（羽毛），其羽茎之义给出尖杆之感；中古英语经古法语得到该词。

items.en: Pinna meant feather, fin or a pointed projecting part.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 指羽毛、鳍或尖出的部分。

items.en: The pointed-stem sense produced pinna as a sharp fastening in late usage.
items.cn: 晚期用法中尖茎之义使 pinna 指尖状固定物。

items.en: Frenchpine and related forms passed the little spike into Norman speech.
items.cn: 法语相关形式把小尖钉传入诺曼语。

items.en: Pin named the sewing needle-like fastener from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 十三世纪起 pin 指类似缝针的固定器。

items.en: Engineering pins, plug pins and the digital PIN code kept the small sharp shape alive.
items.cn: 工程销钉、插脚和数字 PIN 码延续了小而尖的形象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pointed Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers fasteners and fixing words.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁尖物词族；近义组收固定件与固定用语。

entries.definition: The exact point of a pin, then very precise identification.
entries.definitionCN: 针尖点，进而指极精确的定位。

entries.definition: The head of a pin, and anything absurdly tiny.
entries.definitionCN: 针头，以及小得可笑的东西。

entries.definition: A small wing or peak, now the highest point of success.
entries.definitionCN: 原指小尖顶，现指成功的顶点。

entries.definition: A sharp fastener driven by a hammer, larger and rougher.
entries.definitionCN: 用锤敲入的尖钉，更大更粗。

entries.definition: A short flat-headed nail for pinning papers.
entries.definitionCN: 平头小钉，用于钉纸。

entries.definition: A device that grips without piercing.
entries.definitionCN: 夹住而不刺穿的东西。

normalIntro.en: The whole family descends from a feather: thin, pointed, and able to hold two things together.
normalIntro.cn: 整个词族都出自羽毛：细、尖、能把两样东西别在一起。

normal.en: Latin pinna, feather — a quill was nature's first pin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 是羽毛——翎管是大自然的第一枚别针。

normal.en: Pin down does double duty: hold a body still or fix a fact.
normal.cn: pin down 一语双用：按住身体或锁定事实。

normal.en: The pin on a plug and the pin on a badge share one slim metal body.
normal.cn: 插头上的插脚和徽章上的别针共用同一根细金属。

normal.en: PIN codes borrowed the spelling and gave the old word a digital life.
normal.cn: PIN 码借用了拼写，给老词以数字生命。

normal.en: Pinned hopes hang their whole weight on one slim point.
normal.cn: pinned hopes 把全部重量挂在细小的一点上。

abstract.en: One point of contact: the pin holds the world together at its thinnest.
abstract.cn: 一个接触点：别针以最细处撑住世界。

abstract.en: Being pinned is the opposite of freedom — a body, a plan, a blame.
abstract.cn: 被钉住是自由的反面——身体、计划、罪名皆然。

abstract.en: From quill to code, the pin keeps puncturing new meanings.
abstract.cn: 从翎管到代码，别针不断刺出新义。

examples.en: She pinned a rose to his lapel.
examples.cn: 她把一朵玫瑰别在他的翻领上。

examples.en: Rescuers pinned the blame on faulty wiring.
examples.cn: 调查者把责任定位于线路故障。

examples.en: The car pinned his leg against the wall.
examples.cn: 汽车把他的腿抵在了墙上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拼」——把两张纸拼在一起，靠的就是一根小针；pin 就是别针。

root: 拉丁语 pinna / penna（羽毛、羽茎、尖突）经古法语进入中古英语成为 pin；羽毛的细尖形态是所有义项的核心。

sensesIntro.en: One thin point runs from the sewing box through machinery, wrestling mats and bank security to precise identification.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根细尖从针线盒贯穿机械、摔跤垫、银行安全，直至精确定位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp thin point that joins or fixes what it pierces.
core.cn: 核心意象：细而尖的一点，刺入并固定它所穿透之物。

branches.en: a fold of cloth held still
a medal placed on a jacket
shoulders pressed to a mat
a doctor circling the true cause
the same slim rod in a socket and in a code
branches.cn: 同一根细杆：在插座里，也在密码中

intro.en: Pin builds compounds eagerly, from pinhead to pinball, all preserving the small sharp image.
intro.cn: pin 乐于构成复合词，从针头到弹球机，都保留小而尖的形象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin feather root also gave pen and pinnacle, its most famous relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁羽毛词根还派生了 pen 和 pinnacle 这两位最著名的亲戚。

latinEntries.meaning: feather, fin, pointed piece
latinEntries.meaningCN: 羽毛；鳍；尖件

derivatives.zh: 复合词，义为「精确定位」
复合词，义为「针头；极小之物」

definition_zh: 粉红色；粉红色的；略微带刺石竹花；使变红（非正式）
definition_en: a pale red colour, or of that colour, or a garden flower of that colour
core_image: 白色里渗进一点红，像花瓣被霞光染过
scene: 清晨的花店里，一整桶石竹开得正艳，颜色浅得像孩子的脸。The pink carnations filled the shop with light.
sceneCN: 这里是「粉红色的」（第 2 个义项：浅红色）；句意为粉红的康乃馨让店里一片亮色。画面里就是那抹白里透红的花色。

pos.zh: 粉红色；石竹花；极致（the pink)
粉红色的；略带左翼色彩的

derivatives.zh: pink 加 -y 构成，义为「小指；粉粉的」
pink 加 -ish 构成，义为「略带粉色的」
pink 加 -ness 构成，义为「粉色；粉红状态」
pink 加 -ie 构成，义为「小手指」

senses.title: A pale shade of red
senses.definition: a pale red colour
senses.definitionCN: 一种偏浅的红色
senses.example: The walls were painted a soft pink.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁刷成了柔和的粉色。
senses.why: The flower's colour gave its name to the whole shade.
senses.whyCN: 这种花的颜色把名字让给了整个色系。

senses.title: Of a pale red colour
senses.definition: having a pale red colour
senses.definitionCN: 呈浅红色的
senses.example: She wore a pink ribbon in her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她头上系着粉红丝带。
senses.why: The noun of colour turns into its adjective without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 颜色名词直接转为形容词，词形不变。

senses.title: The dianthus flower
senses.definition: a garden plant with fringed, sweet-smelling flowers
senses.definitionCN: 一种开有锯齿边、香气宜人的花的园林植物
senses.example: Old cottage gardens grew pinks along the path.
senses.exampleCN: 老式村舍花园沿小路种着石竹。
senses.why: The word began as the flower itself, before it meant the colour.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指花本身，之后才指颜色。

senses.title: Excellent condition (in the pink)
senses.definition: in very good health or condition
senses.definitionCN: 健康或状态极佳
senses.example: Grandfather is eighty and still in the pink.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父八十岁了，依然精神矍铄。
senses.why: The flower's perfection became a figure for the best possible state.
senses.whyCN: 花的完美成为最佳状态的比喻。

senses.title: To pierce with small holes
senses.definition: to cut cloth or paper with small decorative holes or a zigzag edge
senses.definitionCN: 在布或纸上剪出小孔或锯齿边
senses.example: She pinked the edge of the flag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把旗子边剪成锯齿状。
senses.why: The flower's zigzag petals gave the cutting sense its name.
senses.whyCN: 花瓣的锯齿边给了剪裁义以名字。

senses.title: Having left-wing but moderate views
senses.definition: politically left-leaning but not extreme
senses.definitionCN: 政治上偏左但不极端
senses.example: The magazine was known for its pink politics.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志以其温和左翼立场著称。
senses.why: Red stands for the far left; watering red into pink softens the politics.
senses.whyCN: 红色象征极左；把红兑淡成粉，政治也温和了。

senses.title: A model of perfection
senses.definition: the highest degree or finest example of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最高程度或最佳范例
senses.example: The meal was the pink of perfection.
senses.exampleCN: 这顿饭做得尽善尽美。
senses.why: The flower being the perfect flower made pink the name for perfection.
senses.whyCN: 石竹被视为完美之花，pink 便成了完美的代名词。

intro.en: Pink first named the dianthus flower, whose ragged petals gave a verb for zigzag cutting; the colour name came later, its origin not fully settled.
intro.cn: pink 最初指石竹花，其不齐花瓣产生锯齿剪裁的动词义；颜色名出现较晚，来源尚未完全确定。

items.en: The flower name pink has no certain earlier root; scholars regard its start as obscure.
items.cn: 花名 pink 的更早词根不确定，学者认为其起源晦暗。

items.en: By the fourteenth century pink named the garden flower and a zigzag pierce.
items.cn: 十四世纪 pink 已指这种园林花卉及锯齿状刺孔。

items.en: The pale red colour took the flower's name in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪浅红色借用了花名。

items.en: In the pink for health and the pink of perfection grew from the flower's fame.
items.cn: in the pink 与 the pink of perfection 从花的盛名中生长出来。

items.en: The twentieth century added pink-collar work and the political sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添粉领工作与政治义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the flower family and false friends; the near-meaning group gathers pale reds and health idioms.
note.cn: 形近组收花的词族与假朋友；近义组收浅红各色与健康习语。

entries.definition: The smallest finger, a nursery word built on pink.
entries.definitionCN: 最小的手指，基于 pink 的儿语词。

entries.definition: Somewhat pink, not fully pink.
entries.definitionCN: 略带粉色，还不算纯正粉红。

entries.definition: More pink than something else.
entries.definitionCN: 比另一物更粉。

entries.definition: A stronger, warmer red shade.
entries.definitionCN: 更浓更暖的红色调。

entries.definition: The pink of a face stirred by emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 情绪激动的脸上的粉红。

entries.definition: A pale orange-pink named after the fish.
entries.definitionCN: 以鱼命名的橙粉色。

normalIntro.en: Start from the ragged flower: its jagged petals and pale colour explain every sense.
normalIntro.cn: 从锯齿花出发：参差的花瓣和浅色解释了所有义项。

normal.en: The flower came first, the colour second — pink is a flower turned palette.
normal.cn: 先有花，后有颜色——pink 是变成调色板的花。

normal.en: Pinking shears cut zigzags, copying the petals.
normal.cn: 花边剪剪出锯齿，模仿的正是花瓣。

normal.en: In the pink means flourishing, like a flower at its best.
normal.cn: in the pink 意为兴旺，像开到最好的花。

normal.en: Red diluted with white becomes pink; far-left diluted becomes pink politics.
normal.cn: 红兑白成粉红；极左兑淡成粉红政治。

normal.en: Pinky, the little finger, is the smallest petal of the hand.
normal.cn: 小指 pinky 是手上最小的花瓣。

abstract.en: A cheek after running: blood showing thinly through skin.
abstract.cn: 奔跑后的脸颊：血液薄薄透出皮肤。

abstract.en: Health imagined as the colour of a well-watered garden.
abstract.cn: 把健康想象成一座浇灌得当的花园的颜色。

abstract.en: From petal to politics, pink always means a softened strength.
abstract.cn: 从花瓣到政治，pink 总意味着被柔化的力量。

examples.en: The sky turned pink at sunset.
examples.cn: 日落时天空泛起粉色。

examples.en: He was tickled pink by the birthday surprise.
examples.cn: 生日惊喜让他乐开了花。

examples.en: The tailor pinked every edge before sewing.
examples.cn: 裁缝缝合前把每条边剪成锯齿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「品客」——薯片罐是粉色的，品客一声就是粉红；pink 即粉色。

root: pink 最初指石竹花，词源不确定；锯齿花瓣产生剪裁动词义，十八世纪起浅红色借用花名，另有健康与政治的引申。

sensesIntro.en: One ragged garden flower supplies a colour, a verb of cutting, a state of health, a political tint and a standard of perfection.
sensesIntro.cn: 一朵参差的园林花供出了颜色、剪裁动词、健康状态、政治色调和完美标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pale red light passing through the petals of a carnation.
core.cn: 核心意象：浅红的光透过石竹的花瓣。

branches.en: a wall the colour of dawn
fringed petals along a garden path
an old man lifting his grandson
scissors walking a zigzag line
the same soft red, as colour and as standard
branches.cn: 同一抹柔红：既是颜色也是标准

intro.en: Pink is short and self-contained; English adds only small endings and compounds.
intro.cn: pink 短小自足；英语只加了小的词尾和复合。

latinIntro.en: No Latin relative exists here; the flower name is of uncertain Germanic or obscure origin.
latinIntro.cn: 此处没有拉丁同源词；花名来源不确定，或为日耳曼语源或起源不明。

derivatives.zh: pink 加 -ish，义为「略带粉色的」
pink 加 -y，义为「小指」

definition_zh: 品脱（容量单位）；一品脱装的东西（尤指啤酒）
definition_en: a unit of liquid measure equal to about half a litre, or the amount that a container of this size holds
core_image: 酒馆吧台上那杯带泡沫的大杯啤酒，正好装满一个标准杯
scene: 下班后他走进街角酒馆，要了一大杯冒泡的啤酒。The barman pulled a perfect pint and set it on the counter.
sceneCN: 这里是「一品脱装的东西」（第 2 个义项：一品脱容量的杯中之物）；句意为酒保打出满满一品脱啤酒放在吧台上。画面就是那只标准的大啤酒杯。

derivatives.zh: pint 与 size 合成，义为「小号的；矮小的」，常带玩笑口吻
pint 与 glass 合成，义为「一品脱杯；标准啤酒杯」

senses.title: A unit of liquid volume
senses.definition: a measure of liquid volume equal to eight fluid ounces in the US or about 568 millilitres in the UK
senses.definitionCN: 液量单位，美制约四百七十多毫升，英制约五百六十八毫升
senses.example: The recipe calls for a pint of cream.
senses.exampleCN: 这道菜谱需要一品脱奶油。
senses.why: The old measure was carved on the ale quarts of medieval taverns, and the word kept its official size down the centuries.
senses.whyCN: 这个量制中世纪就刻在酒馆的酒量具上，几个世纪下来词保住了它官方的容量。

senses.title: A glass of beer
senses.definition: a glass of beer served in a container that holds one pint
senses.definitionCN: 装在一品脱容器里的啤酒
senses.example: He bought two pints and found a table by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了两杯啤酒，找了个靠窗的位子。
senses.why: In British pubs the standard beer glass is exactly a pint, so the measure became the drink itself.
senses.whyCN: 英式酒馆的标准啤酒杯正好一品脱，于是量词变成了酒本身。

senses.title: A container of that size
senses.definition: a bottle or carton that holds one pint of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 能装一品脱液体的瓶或盒
senses.example: She opened a pint of ice cream after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她开了一品脱装的冰淇淋。
senses.why: Milk and ice cream are sold in pint containers, so the word points to the package as well as the amount.
senses.whyCN: 牛奶和冰淇淋按品脱盒卖，这个词便既指分量也指包装。

senses.title: The pint measure in idioms
senses.definition: the idea of small size carried by compounds built on pint
senses.definitionCN: 由 pint 构成的复合词所带的小尺寸意味
senses.example: The pint-size guard was the fastest player on the court.
senses.exampleCN: 那个小个子后卫是球场上最快的球员。
senses.why: A single pint is a modest amount, so compounds borrow it to tease someone about being small.
senses.whyCN: 一品脱不算多，复合词便借它来打趣个子小。

intro.en: Pint goes back through Old French to a mark painted on a measuring vessel, so the word is literally a sign that was painted.
intro.cn: pint 经古法语追溯到一个画在量具上的记号，这个词的字面义就是一道画上去的标记。

items.en: Reconstructed *pincta is taken as the feminine past participle of pinctus, meaning painted or marked.
items.cn: 一般认为源自通俗拉丁语重构形式 *pincta，是 pinctus（涂画的）的阴性形式。

items.en: The verb pingere, to paint, underlies the reconstruction; marks on jugs showed how much they held.
items.cn: 动词 pingere（画）是重构形式的来源；罐子上的记号标示容量。

items.en: Old French pinte named both the measure and the marked vessel.
items.cn: 古法语 pinte 既指这个量制，也指带记号的容器。

items.en: The word entered English in the fourteenth century as an official liquid measure.
items.cn: 十四世纪该词进入英语，成为官方液量单位。

items.en: British pub culture fixed the pint glass as the shape of beer, making the measure a drink in daily speech.
items.cn: 英式酒馆文化把品脱杯定型为啤酒的形状，让量词在口语里变成了酒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share pint's sound or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers liquid measures.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pint 音形相近的词；近义组收液量单位。

entries.definition: A horse with patches of two colours; only the sound resembles pint.
entries.definitionCN: 花斑马；与 pint 只是读音相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: A sharp tip or an idea; spelled one letter differently from pint.
entries.definitionCN: 尖端或论点；拼写与 pint 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: Letters or images on paper; shares p-i-n-t letters in a different order.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷的文字图像；字母构成相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Two pints; the older tavern measure from which quart is named.
entries.definitionCN: 两品脱；词源即旧时酒馆的量制。

entries.definition: Eight pints in the imperial system.
entries.definitionCN: 英制中等于八品脱。

entries.definition: The metric unit that replaced pints in most of the world.
entries.definitionCN: 取代品脱的公制单位。

normalIntro.en: A short word of one syllable; memory works on the pub glass and on the painted mark in its etymology.
normalIntro.cn: 单音节短词；记忆抓手是酒馆的杯子与词源里画上去的记号。

normal.en: The medieval jar carried a painted mark — pint is the mark that measured the drink.
normal.cn: 中世纪的罐子上画着记号——pint 就是那道量酒的记号。

normal.en: In Britain, ask for a pint and beer arrives; in America, a pint may be ice cream.
normal.cn: 在英国说 a pint 端上来的啤酒；在美国可能是冰淇淋。

normal.en: Half a gallon makes a quart, two pints make a quart — the ladder of measures climbs by twos.
normal.cn: 两品脱成一夸脱——量制的梯子成倍往上爬。

normal.en: Pint-size teases a small person by measuring him in beer glasses.
normal.cn: pint-size 用啤酒杯给人量身高来打趣个子小。

normal.en: One syllable, five letters, one mark: the whole history of the measure is a painted line.
normal.cn: 一个音节、五个字母、一道记号：整个量制史就是一条画出的线。

abstract.en: Foam climbing over the rim of the pub glass, exactly to the painted line.
abstract.cn: 酒馆杯沿的泡沫正好爬到那道刻线。

abstract.en: A fridge shelf lined with identical pint cartons of milk.
abstract.cn: 冰箱架上排着一排一模一样的品脱牛奶盒。

abstract.en: The mark painted on a jug a thousand years ago still pours drinks tonight.
abstract.cn: 一千年前画在罐上的记号，今晚还在给人打酒。

examples.en: He ordered a pint of bitter and sat down slowly.
examples.cn: 他点了一品脱苦啤酒，慢慢坐下。

examples.en: Add half a pint of stock and let it simmer.
examples.cn: 加半品脱高汤，小火慢炖。

examples.en: The pint-size courier carried boxes bigger than himself.
examples.cn: 那个小个子快递员抱着比自己还大的箱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派恩特」——酒馆里特别给客人打满一杯，派恩特就是一品脱；pint 是量酒的。

root: pint 经古法语 pinte 追至通俗拉丁语重构形式 *pincta（pingere「画」的阴性过去分词），本义是画在量具上的记号；现代义为液量单位。

sensesIntro.en: One painted mark on a medieval jug became a standard measure, then the pub glass of beer, the milk carton and a joke about small size.
sensesIntro.cn: 中世纪陶罐上的一道记号变成标准量制，再变成酒馆的啤酒杯、牛奶盒和一个打趣个子的玩笑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a painted line on a jug that measures exactly one serving.
core.cn: 核心意象：陶罐上一道刻线，量出恰好一份。

branches.en: the official half-litre on paper
the foamy glass in the pub
the carton waiting in the fridge
the teasing ruler for short people
from the statute book to the bar counter

intro.en: Pint has no living prefix or suffix; its family is made of compounds and of measures that grew beside it.
intro.cn: pint 没有活的前后缀；它的词族由复合词和并肩生长的量制词构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb pingere, to paint, is the only classical element in the story, buried in the reconstructed form *pincta.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 pingere（画）是故事里唯一的古典成分，藏在重构形式 *pincta 里。

definition_zh: 管子；导管；烟斗；管乐器；管输送（动词）
definition_en: a tube that carries water or gas, a tube used for smoking, or to send something through such a tube
core_image: 一根空心长管：水从这头进去，从那头出来
scene: 工人蹲在路边的沟里，把一根根长管接到自来水干线上。The workers laid a new pipe under the road to carry water to the village.
sceneCN: 这里是「管子」（第 1 个义项：输送水、气的空心管）；句意为工人们在路下铺设新水管把水引到村里。画面就是那根空心长管。

pos.zh: 用管道输送；以管乐器吹奏

derivatives.zh: pipe 加 line 合成，义为「管道；输油管」
pipe 加 -er 构成的施动名词，义为「吹笛人；管工」
pipe 的动名词，义为「管路；（衣服上的）滚边」
pipe 的过去分词作形容词，义为「用管道输送的」

senses.title: A tube carrying liquid or gas
senses.definition: a tube through which water, gas or oil flows
senses.definitionCN: 水、气或油流过的管子
senses.example: A burst pipe flooded the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 一根爆裂的水管把厨房淹了。
senses.why: Latin pipare described a bird's peep, and the narrow tube took its name from the same thin, hollow sound-image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pipare 描摹鸟叫，细窄的管子因同样的细长中空的声音形象得名。

senses.title: A tube for smoking
senses.definition: a small tube with a bowl, used for smoking tobacco
senses.definitionCN: 带斗的短管，用来吸烟丝
senses.example: Grandfather lit his pipe by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父在炉边点燃烟斗。
senses.why: The tube shape of the instrument transferred to the smoking device, which is literally a small pipe held in the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 管形转指吸烟器具——那其实就是一支叼在嘴上的小管。

senses.title: A tube-shaped musical instrument
senses.definition: a tube that makes music when air is blown through it
senses.definitionCN: 吹气发声的管形乐器
senses.example: The shepherd played a pipe on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 牧羊人在山坡上吹笛。
senses.why: Blowing air through a hollow tube makes a whistling note, which is exactly what the bird-call word described.
senses.whyCN: 向空心管吹气发出哨音，正是鸟叫声那个词所描摹的声音。

senses.title: To carry through a tube
senses.definition: to send water, gas or oil through pipes
senses.definitionCN: 用管道把水、气或油送出去
senses.example: Gas is piped into every apartment in the block.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼的每套公寓都通了管道煤气。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by conversion: the tube itself does the sending.
senses.whyCN: 名词转类成动词：让管子自己去完成输送。

senses.title: To play a tune on pipes
senses.definition: to play music on a pipe or bagpipes
senses.definitionCN: 用管乐器或风笛奏乐
senses.example: A piper piped the guests into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 吹笛人把宾客引进大厅。
senses.why: The instrument name turned into the verb for playing it.
senses.whyCN: 乐器名转成演奏它的动词。

senses.title: To speak in a high voice
senses.definition: to say something in a high, thin voice
senses.definitionCN: 用高而细的声音说话
senses.example: The child piped up with the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子尖着嗓子答了上来。
senses.why: The thin whistle of the tube matches the thin voice of a child, so the sound image moved to speech.
senses.whyCN: 细管的哨音对上孩子尖细的嗓音，声音形象便移到说话上。

senses.title: A cask of wine
senses.definition: a large cask, especially for wine, of about a hundred and twenty gallons
senses.definitionCN: 大酒桶，尤指约一百二十加仑的酒桶
senses.example: The cellar held a pipe of Portuguese wine.
senses.exampleCN: 酒窖里放着一大桶葡萄牙酒。
senses.why: Trade English borrowed the word for a big cask whose shape echoed the tube, though the sizes never matched.
senses.whyCN: 贸易英语借这个词指大桶，形状令人想起管子，尽管容量对不上。

intro.en: Pipe goes back to a Latin word for the chirping of birds, which passed through Old English and Old French to name every narrow hollow tube.
intro.cn: pipe 可追溯到一个拉丁词，本指鸟的啁啾，经古英语与古法语一路命名了所有细长的空心管。

items.en: Pipare meant to chirp or peep, an imitation of a bird's call.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pipare 意为啁啾、唧唧叫，是对鸟鸣的摹声。

items.en: Pipe appeared in Old English for a musical tube and for the sound it made.
items.cn: 古英语已有 pipe，指管乐器及其发出的声音。

items.en: Old French pipe carried the same senses and reinforced the English word.
items.cn: 古法语 pipe 带着同样的义项，强化了英语里的这个词。

items.en: The tube image spread to smoking devices, water conduits and, oddly, large wine casks.
items.cn: 管形意象扩散到吸烟具、输水管，还奇怪地指起大酒桶。

items.en: Conversion produced verbs for conveying through tubes, playing pipes and speaking in thin high voices.
items.cn: 转类造出管道输送、吹奏和尖声说话的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pipe family and sound-alikes; the near-meaning group gathers tubes and conduits.
note.cn: 形近组收 pipe 词族与音近词；近义组收管类物。

entries.definition: One who plays pipes, as in the Pied Piper story.
entries.definitionCN: 吹笛者，如「花衣吹笛人」故事里那样。

entries.definition: A long line of pipes carrying oil or gas over distance.
entries.definitionCN: 远距离输送油气的一长串管道。

entries.definition: An evergreen tree; spelled one letter differently from pipe.
entries.definitionCN: 松树；与 pipe 仅差一个字母，词源无关。

entries.definition: A general hollow cylinder, usually smaller and often for testing or display.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指空心圆管，通常更细，常用于实验或显示。

entries.definition: A flexible tube, especially for spraying water.
entries.definitionCN: 软管，尤指喷水用的。

entries.definition: A channel or pipe that carries water or cables.
entries.definitionCN: 输送水或电缆的管道。

normalIntro.en: One image covers most senses: a hollow tube, and the whistling sound of blowing through it.
normalIntro.cn: 一个意象覆盖多数义项：一根空心管，以及吹过它时的哨音。

normal.en: The bird peeped, the tube whistled, the word pipare imitated both.
normal.cn: 鸟儿唧唧叫，管子呜呜响，pipare 一词摹拟了两者。

normal.en: A pipe has two lives: full of water underground, full of smoke upstairs.
normal.cn: pipe 有两种人生：地下的装满水，楼上的装满烟。

normal.en: Pipe down tells a noisy person to squeeze his voice into a thin pipe again.
normal.cn: pipe down 让吵闹的人把嗓音重新挤成细细的管声。

normal.en: The Pied Piper led rats away with the third sense, the musical tube.
normal.cn: 花衣吹笛人用第三个义项——会唱歌的管子——把老鼠引走了。

normal.en: Gas piped into homes shows the verb doing the tube's work.
normal.cn: 煤气 piped 进家，动词替管子干活。

abstract.en: A long silver tube running under the street, carrying something invisible.
abstract.cn: 一根银色长管在街道下延伸，运送着看不见的东西。

abstract.en: A curl of smoke rising from a curved tube in a fireside hand.
abstract.cn: 炉边一只手里弯管的烟斗升起一缕烟。

abstract.en: A thin high voice rising like a whistle over the classroom noise.
abstract.cn: 一声尖细的嗓音像哨音一样盖过教室的吵闹。

examples.en: The plumber replaced the rusty pipe in minutes.
examples.cn: 水管工几分钟就换掉了生锈的管子。

examples.en: He packed tobacco into his pipe and lit it.
examples.cn: 他把烟丝装进烟斗点着。

examples.en: Water is piped from the reservoir to every farm.
examples.cn: 水经管道从水库送往每个农场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「排扑」——管道排走水、扑灭烟斗火；pipe 就是管子。

root: pipe 源自拉丁语 pipare（鸟啁啾，摹声词），经古英语与古法语进入英语；由「吹管的哨音」引申出管乐器、烟斗、输水管等义。

sensesIntro.en: From a bird's peep to every hollow tube: water pipes, tobacco pipes, organ pipes, and the verbs of sending, playing and squeaking.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一声鸟啼到所有空心管：水管、烟斗、管风琴，以及输送、吹奏和尖声说话的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow hollow tube that carries air, smoke, water or song.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细窄的空心管，送气、送烟、送水、送歌。

branches.en: the conduit under the street
the curved tube by the fire
the shepherd's whistle on the hill
the child's thin voice piping up
the tube and the sending through it

intro.en: Pipe is a short borrowed word that built its family almost entirely with English compounds and conversion.
intro.cn: pipe 是个短小的借词，词族几乎全靠英语复合与转类构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pipare, a bird-call imitation, is the classical seed; English endings did the rest of the building.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pipare 这个摹声词是古典种子；其余的搭建全靠英语词尾。

items.meaning: speak suddenly in a high voice

definition_zh: 投掷；抛；（板球等的）球场；音高；推销；（船的）颠簸；沥青（名词）
definition_en: to throw something, or the level of a sound, a playing field, a sales talk, or a black sticky substance
core_image: 手臂一扬把球掷出——同样的动作在球场、音高、推销和沥青上各掷一次
scene: 投手咬着嘴唇看了一眼本垒，手臂一扬把球掷了出去。The pitcher gave the ball a fast pitch toward the plate.
sceneCN: 这里是「投掷」（第 1 个义项：一次投球的动作）；句意为投手把球快掷向本垒板。画面就是那记干脆的投球。

pos.zh: 投掷；抛；搭（帐篷）；定调；推销
投掷；球场；音高；推销词；沥青

derivatives.zh: pitch 加 -er 构成的施动名词，义为「投手；水罐」
由 pitcher 与 plant 合成，义为「猪笼草；瓶子草」
pitch 的动名词，义为「投掷；（船）纵向颠簸」

senses.title: To throw something
senses.definition: to throw something with force, or to aim it at a target
senses.definitionCN: 用力扔出某物，或朝目标掷去
senses.example: He pitched the crumpled letter into the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把揉皱的信扔进垃圾桶。
senses.why: The basic arm-throwing action is the seed; every later sense plants this throw somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的挥臂投掷是种子；后面的义项都把这记投掷种到别处。

senses.title: To fix a tent or camp
senses.definition: to set up a tent in a place
senses.definitionCN: 在某处支起帐篷
senses.example: We pitched our tent on the ridge before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天黑前我们在山脊上搭好了帐篷。
senses.why: Stakes are driven and lines thrown across the ground, so pitching a camp repeats the throw in pegs and ropes.
senses.whyCN: 打桩、甩绳，扎营的每个动作都是一次投掷的重演。

senses.title: The level of a sound
senses.definition: how high or low a musical note or voice is
senses.definitionCN: 乐音或嗓音的高低程度
senses.example: Her voice dropped to a lower pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音降到更低的音高。
senses.why: A thrown object rises and falls in an arc; a voice thrown into the air lands at a certain height.
senses.whyCN: 掷出的物体划出弧线；抛向空中的嗓音也落在一个高度上。

senses.title: A playing field
senses.definition: a marked area of ground on which a sport is played, used especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 划好界线的运动场地，尤用于英式英语
senses.example: The fans poured onto the pitch after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后球迷涌进球场。
senses.why: The game is pitched onto this square of ground, the same directed throw applied to the playing area itself.
senses.whyCN: 比赛被「掷」上这块场地，定向的投掷挪到了场地本身。

senses.title: A sales talk
senses.definition: a planned talk meant to persuade someone to buy or agree
senses.definitionCN: 为说服他人购买或同意而设计的说辞
senses.example: He gave his pitch in ten sentences and closed the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他用十句话讲完推销词，签下了合同。
senses.why: The seller throws his offer at the buyer like a ball aimed at the strike zone.
senses.whyCN: 卖方像投手瞄准好球区一样，把自己的提议掷向买方。

senses.title: The rise and fall of a ship
senses.definition: the movement of a ship or aircraft when the front rises and falls
senses.definitionCN: 船或飞机的头部起伏的运动
senses.example: The storm made the ferry pitch heavily.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让渡轮颠簸得厉害。
senses.why: The bow rises and falls like an object thrown in an arc, so the motion borrowed the throw's name.
senses.whyCN: 船头像被抛出的物体一样起落，这种运动便借了投掷的名字。

senses.title: A black sticky substance
senses.definition: a thick black sticky substance made from tar, used for waterproofing
senses.definitionCN: 由焦油制成的黑色黏稠物质，用于防水
senses.example: The hull was sealed with pitch before the voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 出海前船壳用沥青封了缝。
senses.why: Pitched wood was thrown in the fire to make waterproof tar; the substance kept the old past-participle name.
senses.whyCN: 把劈开的木头（pitched wood）扔进火里熬出防水焦油，这种物质便沿用了那个过去分词的名字。

intro.en: English pitch is two words sharing one spelling: a Germanic verb of throwing, and an English past participle turned noun for tar.
intro.cn: 英语的 pitch 是两个词共用一个拼法：一个日耳曼源的投掷动词，和一个由过去分词转成名词的焦油词。

items.en: The throwing verb goes back to a reconstructed Germanic root for stabbing or fixing, related to picking.
items.cn: 投掷动词源自一个表示「刺、钉牢」的重构日耳曼词根，与 pick 同源。

items.en: Pitch appeared in Middle English as a verb for throwing and driving in stakes.
items.cn: 中古英语中 pitch 已作动词，指投掷和打桩。

items.en: The substance sense comes from Old English pic, the past participle of piccan, to pitch wood for tar.
items.cn: 物质义来自古英语 pic，即 piccan（劈木熬焦油）的过去分词。

items.en: Sport, sound, sales and ship motion each extended the throw image from the Middle Ages onward.
items.cn: 从中世纪起，体育、声音、推销与船的颠簸各自延伸了投掷意象。

items.en: Modern use keeps all strands alive, from football pitches to elevator pitches.
items.cn: 现代用法把各条线都留着，从足球场到电梯推销词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers pitch's family and look-alikes; the near-meaning group gathers throws, fields and sound levels.
note.cn: 形近组收 pitch 词族与形近词；近义组收投掷、场地与音高词。

entries.definition: The player who throws the ball, and the jug he is named after.
entries.definitionCN: 投手，也指投手一词所借用的水罐。

entries.definition: A small piece of material or ground; spelled one vowel away from pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 补丁；小块地；与 pitch 仅差一个元音字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: A thin rod or a device that turns power on and off; rhymes with pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 细枝或电源开关；与 pitch 押韵，词源无关。

entries.definition: The general word for sending something through the air by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手把东西抛向空中的通称。

entries.definition: A light, careless throw, often upward.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻随意的一抛，常向上。

entries.definition: The marked area for tennis or basketball, the American sibling of pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 网球场或篮球场，是 pitch 在美式英语中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: All senses hang on one arm-throw; remember the throw and the rest follow.
normalIntro.cn: 所有义项都挂在一次挥臂投掷上；记住这记投掷，其余随之而来。

normal.en: One throw, seven lands: the bin, the campsite, the voice, the field, the deal, the ship, the tar.
normal.cn: 一掷七落：垃圾桶、营地、嗓音、球场、生意、船身、焦油。

normal.en: Pitch black is as dark as the tar sense of the word.
normal.cn: pitch black 与该词的焦油义一样黑。

normal.en: The pitcher of water and the pitcher of baseball share one family tree.
normal.cn: 水罐和棒球投手同属一棵家谱树。

normal.en: A sales pitch throws the deal at you; catch it or duck.
normal.cn: 推销词把生意掷向你；接住，或者躲开。

normal.en: High pitch is a note thrown high into the air.
normal.cn: 高音是被高高抛进空中的音符。

abstract.en: An arm swings back, then whips forward — the whole word lives in that swing.
abstract.cn: 手臂后摆再猛然前挥——整个词都活在这一挥里。

abstract.en: A ship's bow lifting and dropping on grey waves, again and again.
abstract.cn: 船头在灰浪上一起一落，反复不止。

abstract.en: Black tar bubbling in a fire of split wood, sealing the seams of a hull.
abstract.cn: 劈开的木头在火里熬出冒泡的黑焦油，封住船壳的缝。

examples.en: Pitch the ball to me and I'll catch it.
examples.cn: 把球抛给我，我来接。

examples.en: The singer hit every note at exactly the right pitch.
examples.cn: 歌手把每个音都唱在准确的音高上。

examples.en: Her pitch for the new app won over the investors.
examples.cn: 她对新应用的推销打动了投资人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈瞧」——一球劈手掷出，瞧它落在球场还是音阶；pitch 就是掷。

root: pitch（投掷义）源于日耳曼语系表示「刺、钉」的动词（中古英语 picchen），与 pick 相关；pitch（沥青义）来自古英语 pic，是 piccan（劈木熬焦油）的过去分词；两词拼法巧合重合。

sensesIntro.en: One throwing arm explains a battlefield of meanings: the ball, the tent, the note, the field, the deal, the ship and the tar.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条挥掷的手臂解释了一片意义战场：球、帐篷、音符、场地、生意、船身与焦油。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm throwing something with force toward a chosen spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条手臂用力把某物掷向选定的地点。

branches.en: the letter tossed into the bin
tent ropes thrown across the grass
a note landing at its height
the offer hurled at the buyer
the arc of a throw and the arc of a ship's bow
branches.cn: 投掷的弧线与船头的弧线

intro.en: Pitch carries no productive affixes; its family is built from conversion, compounds and one agentive suffix.
intro.cn: pitch 没有能产性词缀；词族靠转类、复合和一个施动后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Germanic roots dominate; Latin contributes nothing to this word family.
latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼词根主导；拉丁语在这个词族里毫无贡献。

definition_zh: 怜悯；同情；遗憾的事；可怜（动词）
definition_en: a feeling of sorrow for the troubles of another person, or an unfortunate situation, or to feel this sorrow
core_image: 隔着一道栏杆俯身看向下面的苦，心被轻轻拧了一下
scene: 她隔着医院玻璃看见老人独自吃饭，心里一阵发紧。She felt deep pity for the old man who had no visitors.
sceneCN: 这里是「怜悯」（第 1 个义项：为他人的苦难感到难过）；句意为她对那位无人探望的老人深感同情。画面就是那颗被轻轻拧住的心。

derivatives.zh: pity 加 -ful 构成的形容词，义为「值得怜悯的；可怜的」，也可指「少得可怜的」
pity 加否定后缀 -less，义为「无情的；没有怜悯心的」
pity 加 -able 构成的形容词，义为「可悲的；应受怜悯的」
pitiless 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「无情地」

senses.title: Sorrow for another's suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of sorrow and care caused by someone else's suffering
senses.definitionCN: 由他人苦难引起的难过与关切
senses.example: She looked at the refugees with pity.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀同情地望着难民。
senses.why: Latin pius described devotion and dutiful care, and the feeling of mercy grew from that duty of the heart.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pius 指虔诚与尽责的关怀，怜悯之情正从这颗尽本分的心里长出来。

senses.title: Something regrettable
senses.definition: an unfortunate situation that deserves regret
senses.definitionCN: 令人惋惜的不幸情形
senses.example: It's a pity you missed the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 你错过了那场音乐会，真可惜。
senses.why: When misfortune is small, the heavy word softens into polite regret about circumstances rather than people.
senses.whyCN: 当不幸很轻微，这个沉重的词便软化为对事情的客套惋惜，不再指向人。

senses.title: To feel sorrow for someone
senses.definition: to feel pity for a person
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有怜悯之情
senses.example: I don't want my friends to pity me.
senses.exampleCN: 我不希望朋友们可怜我。
senses.why: The noun of feeling became a verb by conversion: to pour that sorrow onto someone.
senses.whyCN: 情感名词转类成动词：把这份难过倾到某个人身上。

senses.title: Mercy shown in action
senses.definition: kindness that forgives or helps when punishment or indifference would be normal
senses.definitionCN: 本可惩罚或漠然时施予的宽恕或帮助
senses.example: The judge took pity on the young offender and gave him community work.
senses.exampleCN: 法官对年轻被告动了慈悲，判他做社区服务。
senses.why: Take pity on keeps the old religious colour: mercy as a duty of the devout heart.
senses.whyCN: take pity on 保留着古老的宗教色彩：慈悲是虔敬之心的本分。

senses.title: Excessive self-concern
senses.definition: unhealthy concern for one's own troubles, as in self-pity
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的不幸过分在意，如 self-pity
senses.example: He drowned himself in self-pity after losing.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉之后他泡在自怜里出不来。
senses.why: The same sorrow turned inward on the self becomes a weakness rather than a virtue.
senses.whyCN: 同一种难过转向自身，就从美德变成了软弱。

intro.en: Pity descends from Latin pius, the word for devout, dutiful care, passing through piety's family before landing on sorrow for strangers.
intro.cn: pity 源自拉丁语 pius（虔诚、尽责的关怀），先与 piety 同族，后来落在对陌生人的悲悯上。

items.en: Pius meant devoted and dutiful, both to gods and to family; pietas named the duty itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pius 意为虔敬尽责，既对神明也对家人；pietas 指这份本分。

items.en: Pietas became misericordia's rival in meaning, shifting from duty toward mercy.
items.cn: pietas 的含义从本分滑向慈悲，与 misericordia 争锋。

items.en: Old French pité carried the sense of compassion and mercy into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 pité 带着同情与慈悲之义进入罗曼语。

items.en: Pity entered English around the thirteenth century with the same religious warmth.
items.cn: 约十三世纪 pity 带着同样的宗教温度进入英语。

items.en: The word split into deep compassion, polite regret and the inward trap of self-pity.
items.cn: 现代英语里它分成深切的同情、客套的惋惜与自怜的 inward 陷阱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the piety family; the near-meaning group gathers words of compassion and regret.
note.cn: 形近组收 piety 词族；近义组收同情与惋惜的词。

entries.definition: Devotion to religion; the sibling word that kept the devout sense.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教上的虔诚；保留了虔敬义的兄弟词。

entries.definition: Devoutly religious, often now with a hint of hypocrisy.
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的，如今常带伪善意味。

entries.definition: Not pious; disrespectful toward the sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 不虔敬的；对神圣不敬的。

entries.definition: Sorrow that moves you to help, a step beyond merely feeling pity.
entries.definitionCN: 促使你伸出援手的悲悯，比单纯的怜悯更进一步。

entries.definition: Sharing another's feelings, especially in support and comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 体恤他人的感受，尤指支持与安慰。

entries.definition: Kindness that withholds deserved punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 免除应得惩罚的仁慈。

normalIntro.en: The word family is small and regular; memory rides on the link between pity, pious and piety.
normalIntro.cn: 词族小而规整；记忆抓手在 pity、pious、piety 三词的血脉联系。

normal.en: Pity and piety share one Latin heart: the dutiful, caring heart.
normal.cn: pity 与 piety 同一颗拉丁心脏：尽责而关爱的心。

normal.en: Take pity on keeps the old religious act of mercy alive in modern speech.
normal.cn: take pity on 让古老的宗教慈悲之举活在现代口语里。

normal.en: Pitiful can praise an object of pity or scold a pityingly small amount.
normal.cn: pitiful 既可形容可怜的对象，也可斥责少得可怜的数量。

normal.en: Pitiless is the dark twin: the heart that refuses to soften.
normal.cn: pitiless 是黑暗的双生子：拒绝变软的心。

normal.en: What a pity shrinks the great word down to polite everyday regret.
normal.cn: What a pity 把大词缩小成客套的日常惋惜。

abstract.en: A hand reaching over a railing toward someone below, unable to fully help.
abstract.cn: 一只手越过栏杆伸向下方的人，却无法全力施救。

abstract.en: The heart squeezed gently, once, by another person's misfortune.
abstract.cn: 他人的不幸让心被轻轻拧了一下。

abstract.en: A mirror turned inward: the same sorrow pointed at yourself.
abstract.cn: 一面朝内的镜子：同样的悲伤对准了自己。

examples.en: She took pity on the stray cat and fed it daily.
examples.cn: 她可怜那只流浪猫，每天喂它。

examples.en: It's a pity that the old theatre was demolished.
examples.cn: 老剧院被拆掉，实在可惜。

examples.en: His answer dripped with self-pity and satisfied no one.
examples.cn: 他的回答满是自怜，谁也没安慰到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈题」——看见他答不出题被劈头责骂，心生怜悯；pity 就是可怜。

root: pity 源自拉丁语 pius（虔敬、尽责的）及其名词 pietas，经古法语 pité 进入英语；词义由「宗教性的仁慈本分」转为「对他人的怜悯」。

sensesIntro.en: A devout heart's duty became mercy for strangers, then polite regret for small misfortunes, and finally the inward trap of self-pity.
sensesIntro.cn: 虔敬之心的本分变成对陌生人的慈悲，再变成对小不幸的客套惋惜，最后成了自怜的 inward 陷阱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a caring heart bent toward another person's suffering.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗关爱之心俯向他人的苦难。

branches.en: sorrow for the refugee's long walk
the missed train, politely mourned
the judge's mercy in the courtroom
the sorrow curled around oneself
from great suffering to small regret

intro.en: Pity keeps a small but orderly Latin family: feelings that face outward or inward, and suffixes that grade them.
intro.cn: pity 的拉丁词族小而整齐：情感或向外或向内，词缀给它们分级。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root pius feeds the whole family; every ending is English or French in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族由拉丁词根 pius 供血；所有词尾都出自英语或法语。

definition_zh: 比萨饼；意大利薄饼
definition_en: a flat round Italian bread base covered with tomato, cheese and other toppings and baked in an oven
core_image: 圆饼上铺满番茄、奶酪和浇头，从砖炉里端出来还冒着热气
scene: 深夜的厨房里，他从纸盒里抽出最后一块还温热的饼。He reheated the leftover pizza for a midnight snack.
sceneCN: 这里是「比萨饼」（第 1 个义项：一种意式烤饼）；句意为他把剩下的比萨加热当宵夜。画面就是那块铺满浇头的圆饼。

derivatives.zh: pizza 加意大利语后缀 -eria 构成，义为「比萨店」
意大利语借词，义为「做比萨的师傅」

senses.title: The Italian baked dish
senses.definition: a flat round bread baked with tomato, cheese and toppings
senses.definitionCN: 铺了番茄、奶酪和浇头烤成的圆形薄饼
senses.example: We shared a large pizza with mushrooms and ham.
senses.exampleCN: 我们分吃了一个大个的蘑菇火腿比萨。
senses.why: The word named the southern Italian street food and travelled with emigrants around the world.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本指南意大利的街头吃食，随移民走遍世界。

senses.title: A serving or whole pie
senses.definition: one whole pizza, ordered or baked as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个单位订购或烤制的一整个比萨
senses.example: Two pizzas should be enough for six people.
senses.exampleCN: 两个比萨够六个人吃了。
senses.why: The dish name doubles as a counting unit, like cake or pie in English eating speech.
senses.whyCN: 菜名兼任计数单位，就像英语饮食口语里的 cake 或 pie。

senses.title: Pizza as a shared occasion
senses.definition: the informal meal or event built around eating pizza together
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一起吃比萨展开的随意聚餐
senses.example: Movie night means pizza and bad films.
senses.exampleCN: 电影之夜就意味着比萨和烂片。
senses.why: Because the food is cheap, shareable and casual, its name came to stand for the easy gathering itself.
senses.whyCN: 这种食物便宜、可分食、随意，它的名字便代表了那种轻松的聚会本身。

intro.en: Pizza is an Italian dialect word of uncertain deeper origin, first recorded in Naples and carried worldwide by emigration.
intro.cn: pizza 是个意大利方言词，更深的来源不确定，最早见于那不勒斯，随移民传遍世界。

items.en: The word appears in Neapolitan dialect in the tenth-century Latinised form picea, maybe linked to pitta bread.
items.cn: 该词见于那不勒斯方言，十世纪拉丁化形式为 picea，可能与皮塔饼有关。

items.en: Some link it to Latin pinsere, to pound dough; others to a Lombardic word for bite; no theory is certain.
items.cn: 有人把它联系到拉丁语 pinsere（捣面团），也有人联系伦巴第语的「咬」；诸说均无定论。

items.en: In nineteenth-century Naples the modern tomato pizza took shape as street food.
items.cn: 十九世纪的那不勒斯，现代番茄比萨作为街头食品成形。

items.en: Italian emigrants carried pizzerias to America, where the dish conquered global taste.
items.cn: 意大利移民把比萨店带到美洲，这道菜征服了全球味蕾。

items.en: English borrowed the word unchanged, pluralising it with a plain -s.
items.cn: 英语原样借用该词，只加了普通的 -s 构成复数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers look-alikes and the Italian food family; the near-meaning group gathers shareable flat foods.
note.cn: 形近组收形近词与意大利食物家族；近义组收可分享的扁平食物。

entries.definition: The shop where pizza is made and sold.
entries.definitionCN: 制作并出售比萨的店。

entries.definition: A round Middle Eastern flatbread; close in sound and possibly in distant history, but a different food.
entries.definitionCN: 中东圆形面饼；读音相近、来历或有远亲，但是另一种食物。

entries.definition: An open town square in Italy; one letter apart from pizza and unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利的城镇广场；与 pizza 仅差一个字母，意义无关。

entries.definition: Any thin flat bread baked without rising agents.
entries.definitionCN: 各种不加发酵剂烤成的扁平面包。

entries.definition: An Italian folded turnover, pizza's closed cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 意式对折烤饼，比萨的「合上盖」亲戚。

entries.definition: A French savoury tart with egg filling, served in the same casual way.
entries.definitionCN: 法式咸蛋挞，同样以随意的场合上桌。

normalIntro.en: One image and one borrowed word: memory leans on the picture and the Italian shop suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 一个意象、一个借词：记忆靠画面和意大利语的店名后缀。

normal.en: Pizza, pizzeria, pizzaiolo: the food, the shop, the man who makes it.
normal.cn: pizza、pizzeria、pizzaiolo：食物、店、做饼的师傅。

normal.en: Piazza is the square, pizza is the pie — one letter separates the two Italian icons.
normal.cn: piazza 是广场，pizza 是大饼——一个字母隔开两件意大利象征。

normal.en: The plural is plain English: two pizzas, no fuss.
normal.cn: 复数是普通英语：two pizzas，毫不费劲。

normal.en: Deep-pan or thin-crust, the word covers every thickness.
normal.cn: 厚底或薄脆，这个词一视同仁。

normal.en: Pizza night means the gathering, not just the dish.
normal.cn: pizza night 指的是那场聚会，不止是那块饼。

abstract.en: A steaming circle pulled from a brick oven, cheese stretching as a slice lifts.
abstract.cn: 砖炉里端出的热气腾腾的圆饼，掀起一角时奶酪拉出丝。

abstract.en: A square cardboard box, opened at midnight on a sofa.
abstract.cn: 深夜沙发上打开的方形纸盒。

abstract.en: Hands reaching into the middle of the table, all at once.
abstract.cn: 几只手同时伸向桌子中央。

examples.en: A hot pizza arrived twenty minutes after we ordered.
examples.cn: 我们下单二十分钟后，热比萨送到了。

examples.en: The pizzeria on the corner sells pizza by the slice.
examples.cn: 街角的比萨店按块卖比萨。

examples.en: Nothing ends a road trip better than late-night pizza.
examples.cn: 没有什么比深夜的比萨更能给自驾游收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必萨」——聚餐必点比萨，一萨不够再来一萨；pizza 就是比萨饼。

root: pizza 为意大利（那不勒斯）方言借词，更深词源不确定：或联系拉丁语 pinsere（捣制面团），或联系 pitta（皮塔饼）一类扁面包，诸说并存，未成定论。

sensesIntro.en: A borrowed dialect word names the Neapolitan street food, then the whole pie, then the casual gathering built around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个借来的方言词先命名那不勒斯的街头吃食，再指一整份饼，最后指围绕它的随意聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round flat pie with toppings, hot from the oven.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张铺满浇头的圆形扁饼，刚出炉还热着。

branches.en: tomato and cheese on baked bread
the whole pie in the cardboard box
friends around the open box
branches.cn: 围着打开纸盒的朋友们

branches.en: the street corner of Naples reborn worldwide
branches.cn: 那不勒斯街角的世界重生

branches.en: from counting pies to sharing the evening

intro.en: Pizza is a whole borrowed word; its family is Italian, using Italian suffixes for the shop and the maker.
intro.cn: pizza 是整词借入；词族是意大利的，用意大利后缀造出店名和师傅名。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is firmly established; even the Italian roots remain debated.
latinIntro.cn: 没有任何拉丁成分确证成立；连意大利语内部词根仍有争议。

definition_zh: 地方；地点；位置；名次；放置（动词）
definition_en: a particular area or position, a position in a competition, or to put something somewhere
core_image: 手掌摊开，把一样东西轻轻放在它该在的位置
scene: 她把钥匙稳稳放在玄关的小碟里，动作轻得没有一点声音。She placed the keys gently in the little dish by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「放置」（第 5 个义项：把东西放在某处）；句意为她把钥匙轻轻放在门边小碟里。画面就是那只摊开的手掌。

derivatives.zh: place 加 -ment 构成的名词，义为「安置；实习安排」
re-（重新）+ place，义为「取代；替换」
dis-（离开）+ place，义为「使离开原位；取代」
拉丁借词（字面「我将使你愉快」），义为「安慰剂」

senses.title: A particular area or spot
senses.definition: a particular part of space where something is or can be
senses.definitionCN: 某物所在或可在的特定空间
senses.example: This café is my favourite place in town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆是我在城里最爱的地方。
senses.why: Greek plateia named a wide street, and Latin platea narrowed it to any particular spot in a town.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 plateia 指宽阔的街道，拉丁语 platea 把它收窄为城里任何特定的位置。

senses.title: A position in space or a series
senses.definition: the position something or someone occupies in space, order or a competition
senses.definitionCN: 事物或人在空间、次序或竞赛中占据的位置
senses.example: She took third place in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 她在决赛里得了第三名。
senses.why: A spot in the world becomes a spot in a ranking: the same slot, measured socially.
senses.whyCN: 世界上的位置变成排名里的位置：同一个格位，换成社会度量。

senses.title: A role or duty
senses.definition: a person's proper position in society or in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在社会或局面中应有的位置
senses.example: He knew his place in the family business.
senses.exampleCN: 他清楚自己在家族企业里的位置。
senses.why: The physical slot turns social: knowing your place is knowing which slot the world assigns you.
senses.whyCN: 物理的格位转向社会：知道自己的本分就是知道世界给你划定的格子。

senses.title: A home or abode
senses.definition: the house or building where someone lives
senses.definitionCN: 某人居住的房子或建筑
senses.example: Come over to my place tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚来我家。
senses.why: The widest sense, any spot, shrinks to the most personal spot of all, where you live.
senses.whyCN: 最宽泛的「任何地点」缩到最私人的地点——你住的地方。

senses.title: To put something somewhere
senses.definition: to put something in a particular position, often carefully
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到特定位置，常指细致地放
senses.example: He placed the vase exactly in the centre.
senses.exampleCN: 他把花瓶精确地放在正中央。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by conversion: to give a thing its place.
senses.whyCN: 名词转类成动词：给一件东西安排它的位置。

senses.title: To arrange or set up
senses.definition: to arrange for something to be done or to find someone a position
senses.definitionCN: 安排做成某事或为某人找到位置
senses.example: The agency placed her with an engineering firm.
senses.exampleCN: 中介替她在一家工程公司安排了职位。
senses.why: Placing a person means putting them into a social slot, extending the verb to people and jobs.
senses.whyCN: 给某人「安放位置」就是把动词的触角伸向人和职位。

intro.en: Place walks from a Greek word for a broad street through Latin and French before settling in English as spot, rank and verb.
intro.cn: place 从一个希腊语的「宽阔街道」出发，经拉丁语和法语，最后在英语里落脚为地点、名次和动词。

items.en: Plateia hodos meant broad way; the feminine adjective alone became the noun.
items.cn: plateia hodos 意为宽阔的路；阴性形容词单独成名。
